basis: Lowest publicly bookable room per night, two adults one room, gross of tax, collected direct from each hotel's own booking engine over a full forward year. Cleaned on the desk convention: nights above GBP10,000 dropped, then nights above 2.5x the property's own median dropped.
cautions: A month with nothing bookable is not necessarily a closed month. Several seasonal hotels had not loaded next season's inventory when this was collected. The inference only runs the other way: a hotel bookable in all twelve months is demonstrably year-round.

Annual medians only compare between properties with similar bookable-night coverage. Passalacqua prices at 2.7 times Villa d'Este in August yet sits below it on the year, because it sells 85 nights weighted into its cheap months.
A flat month is usually season-band pricing, which is how these hotels sell, not a fault. The exception is a flat month far outside the property's own range.
These are lead-in rates, not achieved ADR. No property in this set publishes an achieved rate.
figures_basis: The headline figures each hotel discloses, or that can be computed from what it discloses. Every row carries its own basis and its evidence class: filed, from a statutory account; press, from unaudited reporting; interview, from a named manager or owner on the record; derived, computed here from two disclosed figures; modelled, from the portal's own estimated profit and loss for that hotel rather than the hotel's own; note, a statement of what does not exist. The Continental filed figures reach us through registry aggregators surfacing a deposited filing rather than through the filed document itself, and are snippet-grade until a paid registry copy is bought. A blank is a blank: most of this set publishes nothing beyond a rate.
type_basis: Each property is grouped by its setting: an inland estate or demesne, a sea coast or island, a lake shore, an alpine valley, or a palace, town or village. The grouping is the portal's own reading of the setting each research pack records, not a classification any of these hotels publishes.
vat_note: Accommodation VAT differs by country: 20% United Kingdom, 10% France Italy Austria Spain, 13% Greece, 13.5% Ireland. The desk's divide-by-1.20 is a United Kingdom constant and does not hold outside it.

villas_basis: Whole-house self-catering lets on the Son Bunyola estate, sold per night with a minimum stay of three nights in the shoulder and four in peak, and no meals. They are not comparable to a nightly room rate and are kept out of the hotel index. They matter here because a hotel with separately-sold houses beside it is the shape of the subject. They clear EUR900 to EUR1,280 a bedroom against a hotel median of EUR1,020 a room, so the house limb earns on space and length of stay rather than on a rate premium — and the four-bedroom house clears least per bedroom of the three.
